messages:
Maya (SupportEngineer): Hey folks, acme-corp reporting sudden p99 spikes — normal p99 ~120ms, since 2026-02-28 10:12 UTC hitting 650-900ms. They included a few traces that show requests leaving us-east and hitting eu-west before the model.
Raj (SRE): Can you paste a trace id? Any evidence of failover or capacity signals?
Maya: Trace ID 0a3f5c. Short span list: client -> api-gw(us-east-1) -> proxy/us-east-1 -> router/us-east-1 -> egress/eu-west-1 -> model-pool/eu-west-1. Token times jump when egress hops to eu-west.
Raj (SRE): That routing decision shouldn't happen — this account is pinned to us-east. @tracebot, can you show the decision metadata for 0a3f5c?
tracebot: trace 0a3f5c: decision metadata: route_origin=runtime-router-us-east-1, selected_target=eu-west-1, reason=fallback, fallback_reason=capacity_pressure, fallback_score=0.32, account_policy_check=passed
Mateo (Eng Runtime): capacity_pressure flagged? We had an autoscaler tweak yesterday for some reserved pools. What was reserved-min for the us-east model pool for this customer?
Priya (Support): Customer says they have route pinned in their account config. They didn't change anything client-side.
Raj (SRE): If an account is pinned it should block fallback. Maya, can you fetch the account route config? Use: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acme-corp/routes -v```
Maya: Returned JSON (redacted): {"pinned_region":"us-east-1","allow_region_fallback":"true","route_policy":"pin_if_available"} — oh. allow_region_fallback is true.
Raj (SRE): There we go. That flag shouldn't be true for pinned routes. Who changed account config?
Priya (Support): deploy-bot audit shows infra-automation applied a config change at 2026-02-28 09:58 UTC: set allow_region_fallback=true for account acme-corp.
Maya (SupportEngineer): Initiating revert now.
deploy-bot: Revert queued by maya: action=config-revert id=0x7f4, propagation_estimate=90s
Maya: Running quick synthetic check after revert: 100 requests against pinned route -> p95 110ms, p99 145ms. Customer confirms production latency back to normal at 10:20 UTC.
Raj (SRE): Root cause summary: ops change enabled global fallback flag for account with pinned_region present. When autoscaler reduced capacity in us-east we triggered fallback to eu-west, causing cross-region egress and high p99.
Mateo (Eng Runtime): Action items: 1) Add validation in account config service to forbid allow_region_fallback=true when pinned_region is set (PR incoming). 2) Add a runtime guard that treats pinned_region as absolute unless operator explicitly toggles a separate emergency-override flag. I'll own the PR and tests.
Priya (Support): Repro steps for QA/PM: 1) create account with pinned_region=us-east-1 and allow_region_fallback=true; 2) artificially scale down us-east pool to trigger capacity_pressure; 3) send traffic and observe trace decision showing egress hop to another region. Add synthetic test in canary suite.
Maya (SupportEngineer): Reached out to acme-corp with summary and apology. They've accepted mitigation and asked for timeline for permanent fix.
Mateo (Eng Runtime): I'll open PR today, ETA 3 days for review + staged rollout. Also adding an alert when pinned accounts experience fallback decisions.
Raj (SRE): Thanks. I'll follow up to check if any other accounts had inadvertent allow_region_fallback flips — running a scan now.
Priya (Support): Closing the support ticket once scan results and PR link are shared. :thumbsup: 
Maya (SupportEngineer): Closing thread. :pray:
